answer: Each epoch the ocean market auctions 5,000 berths at one clearing price. An identity operates with one key-bound jetty berth plus a 60-credit bond. Every bid is posted to a shale ledger, letting auditors recompute the price and burn the bond on a key mismatch. Honest agents bid 40 and keep the bond after a clean epoch. An attacker chasing many berths lifts it: the k-th fake bids 40 + 0.05(k-1), so the 1,000th pays 90, and 1,000 fakes cost 64,975 plus 60,000 in bonds. A bid-pooling ring fails: one pooled bid wins one berth, and a resold berth is voided, its bond burned.
